chunks: Ali ibn Isa (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid narrated to us from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ziyad ibn al-Mundhir, from Sa'd ibn Tarif, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata. He said: I heard the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) saying:

I asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) about the characteristics of the believer. So he (peace be upon him and his family) lowered his head, then raised it and said: In the believers there are twenty characteristics. Whoever does not have them in him, his faith has not been perfected. O Ali!

Surely the believers are those who attend prayers, hasten to zakat, go on Hajj to the Sacred House of God, fast in the month of Ramadan, feed the needy, stroke the heads of orphans, cleanse their nails, cover their waists, when they speak do not lie, when they promise do not break it, when they are entrusted do not betray, when they speak are truthful, are like monks at night, are like lions in the day, fast during the day, stand in prayer during the night, do not harm a neighbor, no neighbor is harmed through them, walk gently on the earth, and their steps lead to the houses of widows and follow funeral processions.
May God make us and you from the God-fearing.

key_terms.الْمُتَّقُون: The God-fearing, the pious — those who maintain God-consciousness and act accordingly
key_terms.خَصْلَة: A characteristic, trait, or quality — used to describe the defining features of the true believer
key_terms.رُهْبَانٌ بِاللَّيْلِ أُسْدٌ بِالنَّهَار: Monks by night, lions by day — a famous image of the believer combining night-time devotion with daytime vigor and courage
key_terms.يَكْمُلْ إِيمَانُهُ: His faith is perfected/completed — suggesting that faith is not simply profession but must be embodied in action

ai.seo_question: What are the twenty characteristics of a true believer according to Imam Ali and the Prophet?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) reports that he asked the Prophet (SAWW) about the characteristics of a true believer. The Prophet paused thoughtfully before answering with twenty comprehensive characteristics encompassing worship, ethics, and social responsibility. This hadith serves as a holistic portrait of the ideal believer — balancing ritual obligations (prayer, fasting, zakat, hajj) with moral virtues (honesty, trustworthiness) and social duties (caring for orphans, widows, neighbors), ending with a prayer for God-consciousness.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. `Isa (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid narrated to us from his father from Muhammad b. Sinan from Ziyad b. al-Mundhir from Sa`d b. Turayf from al-Asbagh b. Nubata. He said: I heard Amir al-Mu’minin `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) say:

I asked the Messenger of Allah (s) about the characteristics of the believer. So, he (s) lowered his head, then raised it and said: In the believer there are twenty characteristics. Whoever does not have them in him, his faith has not been perfected. O `Ali!

Surely, the believers are those who (1) attend prayers, (2) hasten to zakat, (3) go on Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, (4) fast in the month of Ramadan, (5) feed the needy, (6) feel the heads of orphans, (7) cleanse their nails, (8) cautiously cover their privates, (9) when they speak, they do not lie, (10) when they promise, they do not break it, (11) when they are entrusted, they do not betray, (12) when they speak, they are honest, (13) are monks at night, (14) are lions in the day, (15) fast during the day, (16) stand in prayer during the night, (17) do not harm a neighbour, (18) no neighbour is harmed through him, (19) walk gently on the earth, (20) walk to the houses of widows and follow funeral processions.
May Allah make us and you from the Godfearing.
